answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity expensive to create and cheap to lose: each new agent must lock a small refundable stake and finish verifiable work before trading, while peers compare behavioral fingerprints across accounts. Like shale layers that record distinct pressure over time, a real history cannot be faked overnight; when a sudden plume of identical accounts wander into the same market at once, the network quarantines them and slashes their stake, so flooding the system costs more than any fake vote can earn.
